JVM internals for Kotlin and Android developers · check

Know Reading bytecode already?

One question for each of the 6 puzzles in this module. A right answer marks that puzzle as passed, so you can jump ahead. A wrong one tells you which puzzle to start with. Nothing is sent anywhere: it's saved in this browser.

Puzzle 5: Where does the arithmetic happen?

A method returns visits - stars. Which instruction list computes it?

Not quite. The inputs must be on the stack before the instruction that uses them runs. Learn it in puzzle 5 →

Not quite. The value pushed first is the left-hand side; this list computes stars - visits. Learn it in puzzle 5 →

Right. The first value pushed sits deeper and is the left-hand side.

Puzzle 6: What does #7 point to?

You rename the field weight to factor and recompile Score. In the constant pool, what changes?

Not quite. The instruction holds an index into the pool, never an address. Learn it in puzzle 6 →

Right. Fields are described by name and descriptor.

Not quite. The name is exactly what the pool keeps, so it can be looked up while the program runs. Learn it in puzzle 6 →

Puzzle 7: Which method does a call run?

Counter.next() is overridable, and a subclass Loud overrides it. A method takes a parameter c: Counter and calls c.next(). You pass it a Loud. Which instruction is in the method's bytecode, and which next() runs?

Right. The declared type picks the instruction; the receiver's class picks the code.

Not quite. invokespecial is for calls that must run one exact method; an overridable call isn't one. Learn it in puzzle 7 →

Not quite. The compiler only knows the declared type, Counter; the object is known only while the program runs. Learn it in puzzle 7 →

Puzzle 8: What did Kotlin write for you?

visit gets a third parameter, note: String = "". You call visit(b, 5) and leave note out. Which mask does visit$default receive?

Right. Bit n is set for argument n.

Not quite. Bit 0 belongs to argument 0, b, which was given. Learn it in puzzle 8 →

Not quite. The mask marks which argument, by position, not how many: bit 2 has the value 4. Learn it in puzzle 8 →

Puzzle 9: Where did my lambda go?

You remove inline from runNow and recompile. What appears in main where the println instructions were?

Right. A plain function receives the lambda as an object.

Not quite. runNow still needs the lambda, so main must build a function object to pass. Learn it in puzzle 9 →

Not quite. Without inline, nothing is copied; the lambda must become an object to be passed. Learn it in puzzle 9 →

Puzzle 10: How does a call find the override?

A class Shout extends Loud and overrides next again with v + 100. A Shout reaches use(c). Which entry does invokevirtual read, and what does use return?

Not quite. The instruction names the method; the receiver's table decides the code. Learn it in puzzle 10 →

Not quite. The copy is made first, then Shout's override replaces that entry. Learn it in puzzle 10 →

Right. Each class's table has its own overrides at the same position.
